Order 
The appellant / ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited (none-appellant No.3 before the Tribunal) has filed this appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 challenging the award dated 29.10.2021 passed in Claim Case No.370/2015 only in respect of quantum of the compensation awarded in favour of respondent No.1 / claimant.

entities.text: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: 02. Respondent No.1 / claimant filed a claim case before the Tribunal claiming compensation on account of death of her son Aqeeb due to a road accident.

According to the claimant on 03.05.2015,

sentences.text: Aqeeb (deceased) along with his maternal uncle, Rafiq was going from Nagda Junction to Daulatabad to attend the marriage.
Rafiq was driving the motorcycle slowly.
When they reached near Betma Road Jubilee Petrol Pump, one motorcycle bearing registration No.MP 09 QJ 1224 dashed his motorcycle due to which they fell down.
Deceased - Aqeeb sustained severe injuries and he was taken to the Aurobindo Hospital, where on 29.05.2015, he succumbed to his injuries.
According to the claimant, the deceased was 23 years of age and was healthy person.
He was having the degree of B.E. and working in EICHER Trucks & Buses, Pithampur as an Assistant Engineer and was earning monthly salary of Rs.19,560/-.
He maintaining himself as well as the claimant, whose husband expired long back, therefore, she claimed Rs.50,00,000/- as compensation.

Non-appellants No.1 & 2 (before the Tribunal) owner and driver of the motorcycle remained ex parte.
03.
The Insurance Company filed a written statement denying the liability to pay compensation.
The learned Tribunal framed seven issues for adjudication.
While answering issues No.1, 2, 3, 4 & 5, the learned Tribunal held that the accident was caused by non-appellant No.2 while driving the motorcycle due to which Aqeeb died.
At the time of accident, non-appellant No.2 was having valid and effective license and it is not a case of contributory negligence.
The claim does not suffer from non-joinder of the parties.

After taking into consideration the law laid down by the Apex Court in the cases of Sarla Verma v/s Delhi Transport Corporation reported in 2009 A.C.J. 1298 SC and National Insurance Company Limited v/s Pranay Sethi & Another (S.L.P. (Civil) No.167335/2014) in respect of income, age and dependency, the learned Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.21,38,420/- in favour of the claimant.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v/s Delhi Transport Corporation reported in 2009 A.C.J. 1298 SC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v/s Pranay Sethi & Another (S.L.P. (Civil) No.167335/2014)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the present appeal is before this Court only on the ground that claimant has failed to prove the income of Rs.19,560/- per month.

04. Shri Manoj Jain, learned counsel for the appellant / Insurance Company submits that the certificate of income, which was produced by the claimant has been disbelieved but the notional income of Rs.18,000/- per month has been taken without any basis.
In the year 2015, the notional income ought to have been taken Rs.10,000/-, therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on a higher side.
05. I have heard learned counsel for the appellant at length and perused the record.
06. The deceased was 23 years' old and having an Engineering Degree.

For an Engineer,
Rs.18,000/- per month has rightly been assessed by the Tribunal even after the certificate in respect of income has been disbelieved.
During the course of arguments, Shri Jain has not disputed that future prospect has not been awarded by the learned Tribunal.
In this case even if income is reduced from Rs.18,000/- to Rs.10,000/-, there would be no change in the total amount of compensation by awarding compensation under the head of future prospects.
The deduction of 50% has rightly been done as only the mother of the deceased was dependent on him.

Looking to the age of the deceased,
multiplier of 18 has rightly been applied, therefore, no case for reduction of compensation is made out in the matter.
Even otherwise, no amount was awarded under future prospect.
I do not find any reason to interfere with the award passed by Tribunal.
With observation as aforesaid, Miscellaneous Appeal stands dismissed.
